result.topic_en: Differential formulas for the variations of the orbital elements (parameter, inclination, node, semi-major axis, eccentricity angle) of a planet perturbed by another planet, with the orbital plane of the perturbed planet taken as the fundamental plane.
result.transcription:
59.
$\partial v = \frac{\cos b^2 \partial\lambda}{\cos i}$
$\sqrt{p} = \frac{ss\partial\lambda}{\cos i . k dt}$
$k\partial t . \partial\sqrt{p} = \frac{s\partial t^2}{\cos i}(X\sin\lambda - Y\cos\lambda) + \frac{ss\,\mathrm{tang}\, i . \partial\lambda . \partial i}{\cos i}$
$= \frac{\mu ss'\partial t^2}{\cos i}\left(\frac{1}{r'^3} - \frac{1}{\varrho^3}\right)\sin(\lambda-\lambda') + \frac{ss\,\mathrm{tang}\, i . \partial\lambda . \partial i}{\cos i}$
Man sieht leicht daß die Fundamentalebne hier willkürlich ist.
Nimmt man die Ebne der Bahn des gestörten Planeten dafür an, so hat
man, wenn man die Länge des störenden, auf die Ebne des gestörten projicirt
durch $w'$, die Breite durch $\beta'$ bezeichnet
$\partial p = \frac{2\mu r r' \cos\beta' \sqrt{p} . k dt}{\odot}\left\{\frac{1}{r'^3} - \frac{1}{\varrho^3}\right\}\sin(v-w')$
$\partial i = \frac{\mu r r' k\partial t . \cos(v-\Omega)}{\odot\sqrt{p}}\left\{\frac{1}{\varrho^3} - \frac{1}{r'^3}\right\}\sin\beta'$
$\partial\Omega = \frac{\mu r r' k\partial t . \sin(v-\Omega)}{\sin i . \odot\sqrt{p}}\left\{\frac{1}{\varrho^3} - \frac{1}{r'^3}\right\}\sin\beta'$

$\frac{1}{a} = \frac{2}{r} - \frac{\partial x^2 + \partial y^2 + \partial z^2}{\odot\partial t^2}$
$\partial\frac{1}{a} = \frac{2}{\odot}(X\partial x + Y\partial y + Z\partial z) = \frac{2\mu}{\odot}\left(\frac{r\partial r}{\varrho^3} - \left(\frac{1}{\varrho^3} - \frac{1}{r'^3}\right) d(xx'+yy'+zz')\right)$
$= \frac{2\mu}{\odot}\left(\frac{r\partial r}{\varrho^3} - \left(\frac{1}{\varrho^3} - \frac{1}{r'^3}\right) d\, rr'\cos \mathrm{dist.ang}\right)$
$= \frac{2\mu}{\odot}\left(\frac{r\partial r}{\varrho^3} - \left(\frac{1}{\varrho^3} - \frac{1}{r'^3}\right)\left\{r'\cos(v-w')\cos\beta' . \partial r - rr'\sin(v-w')\cos\beta'\partial v\right\}\right)$
$= \frac{2\mu}{\odot}\left(\frac{r}{\varrho^3} - \left(\frac{1}{\varrho^3} - \frac{1}{r'^3}\right) r'\cos(v-w')\cos\beta'\right)\partial r - \frac{\partial v . \partial p}{k\partial t . \sqrt{p}}$
$T = \frac{\mu}{\odot}\left(\frac{r}{\varrho^3} - \left(\frac{1}{\varrho^3} - \frac{1}{r'^3}\right) r'\cos(v-w')\cos\beta'\right)$
$V = \frac{\mu}{\odot}\left(\frac{1}{\varrho^3} - \frac{1}{r'^3}\right) rr'\sin(v-w')\cos\beta'$ [?]
$W = \frac{\mu}{\odot}\left(\frac{1}{\varrho^3} - \frac{1}{r'^3}\right) rr'\sin\beta'$ [?]
$\partial\frac{1}{a} = \frac{2\mu}{\odot} dR$
$\partial\mu = \frac{3\mu}{\odot} . a\mu . dR$
$R = \frac{\xi}{r'r'} - \frac{1}{\varrho}$
1) $\partial i = \frac{k\partial t}{\sqrt{p}} . W\cos(v-\Omega)$
2) $\partial\Omega = \frac{k\partial t}{\sin i . \sqrt{p}} . W\sin(v-\Omega)$
3) $\partial p = -2\sqrt{p} . k\partial t . V$
4) $\partial a = -\frac{2aak\partial t}{\sqrt{p}} . T . e\sin(v-\omega) - \frac{2aa\sqrt{p} . k\partial t}{rr} . V$
5) $\partial\varphi = -\sqrt{a} . k\partial t . T\sin(v-\omega) - \frac{2\cos(v-\omega) [?] + e + e\cos(v-\omega)^2 [?]}{\cos\varphi . \sqrt{p}} k\partial t . V$
$= -\sqrt{a} . k\partial t . T\sin(v-\omega) - \frac{\sqrt{a}}{r} . k\partial t . (\cos v + \cos E) . V$
NB. In obigen Entwickelungen ist $dv$ in einem doppelten Sinne genommen,
einmal als Differential von $v$, und zweitens als Element der helioc.
